analysis.title: Friday, November 13, 2026 Daily Market Note (Friday the 13th, Existing Home Sales, PPI)
key_insights: Friday the 13th has been the strongest weekday for the S&P 500 since 1928, averaging +0.09% and positive 58% of the time vs +0.02% and 52% for all other days. The note calls it historical trivia, not causation, and recommends staying invested rather than timing the market.
October existing home sales fell 5.5% MoM to 3.75 million, the lowest since August 2010. Sales declined across most regions. Mortgage rates remain near three-year highs and weigh on housing demand.
Inventory rose to 5.1 months' supply from 4.4 a year ago, but prices remain near record levels, up 0.4% YoY. The note expects housing activity to stay subdued and sees no panacea for affordability.

Consensus for October PPI (8:30 AM ET) is headline +6.6% YoY, driven largely by fuel prices, with core PPI at +5.0% YoY. A higher-than-expected core figure would reinforce concerns that cost pressures are spreading beyond energy.
Following Tuesday's hotter than expected CPI, the note expects this week's inflation reports to strengthen the case for a 25 bp Fed rate hike on December 9, followed by an extended pause.

Cleveland Fed President Hammack, who dissented in favor of a 25 bp hike at last month's FOMC, rejected the idea of a 50 bp hike. She wants restrictive policy, cites broadening inflation pressures, but does not see the Fed as behind the curve and prefers smaller moves. Gov. Waller raised the 50 bp idea earlier in the week.
The PHLX Semiconductor Index fell only 0.3% yesterday despite an abrupt leadership change at NVIDIA (CEO resignation). Excluding NVIDIA, semiconductors gained 2.3% and are up 19% week-to-date.

The note says the AI infrastructure buildout continues to drive chip demand with high visibility into 2027. Consensus expects 67% industry EPS growth in 2027, and the note stays positive on the Tech sector overall.
